problem.summary: 缺乏通用的视频描述符，难以统一处理大规模视频分析任务（如动作识别、场景分类等）。

motivation.summary: 互联网视频爆炸式增长，需要一种通用、紧凑、高效且简单的视频特征描述符，以支持搜索、推荐、排序等应用。

core_idea.summary: 使用深度3D卷积网络（3D ConvNets）在大规模监督视频数据集上学习时空特征，提出C3D（Convolutional 3D）特征。

method.summary: 设计并训练一个具有8个卷积层、5个池化层和2个全连接层的3D卷积网络，所有卷积核均为3×3×3，在Sports-1M数据集上训练，提取fc6层激活作为视频特征。

experiments.summary: 在6个基准数据集（Sports-101、UCF101、ASLAN、YUPENN、UMD、Object）上评估C3D特征，与现有最佳方法比较，并进行架构搜索、紧凑性、效率等分析。

claims.claim: 3D ConvNets比2D ConvNets更适合时空特征学习。
具有小3×3×3卷积核的同构架构是3D ConvNets的最佳架构之一。
C3D特征在多个基准上优于或接近现有最佳方法，且紧凑、高效、简单。

limitations.limitation: C3D需要与iDT等特征结合才能在某些任务上超越双流网络；在Sports-1M和UCF101上未达到绝对最佳；对第一人称视角物体识别效果一般。

nodes.title: 3D卷积与池化
nodes.label: 核心操作
nodes.summary: 3D卷积和池化操作在时空维度上进行，能够同时建模外观和运动信息，而2D操作仅在空间维度进行。
nodes.description: 3D卷积核在视频体积上滑动，输出另一个体积，保留时间信息；2D卷积在多帧上操作会输出图像，丢失时间信息。3D池化类似，在时空维度上降采样。

nodes.title: 架构搜索
nodes.label: 实验设计
nodes.summary: 在UCF101上搜索最佳3D卷积核时间深度，发现3×3×3同构架构表现最佳。
nodes.description: 固定空间感受野为3×3，仅变化卷积核时间深度d。实验了同构深度（所有层相同d）和变化深度架构。结果表明深度-3（d=3）的同构架构在准确率和参数效率上最优。

nodes.title: C3D网络架构
nodes.label: 模型定义
nodes.summary: 最终的C3D网络包含8个3×3×3卷积层、5个池化层（pool1为1×2×2）、2个4096单元的全连接层和softmax输出层。
nodes.description: 所有3D卷积滤波器为3×3×3，步长1×1×1。池化层为2×2×2，步长2×2×2，除了pool1为1×2×2以保留早期时间信息。输入为16帧112×112的视频片段。

nodes.title: 训练过程
nodes.label: 训练细节
nodes.summary: 在Sports-1M数据集上从头训练C3D，使用SGD，初始学习率0.003，每150K迭代除以2，训练1.9M迭代。
nodes.description: 从每个训练视频中随机提取5个2秒片段，调整为128×171，随机裁剪为16×112×112并水平翻转。小批量大小为30。

nodes.title: 特征提取
nodes.label: 推理过程
nodes.summary: 将视频分割为16帧片段（8帧重叠），通过C3D网络提取fc6激活，平均后L2归一化，得到4096维视频描述符。
nodes.description: 在推理时，视频被分成重叠的16帧片段，每个片段通过网络得到fc6层激活，所有片段的激活取平均，然后L2归一化，形成最终的C3D视频特征。

nodes.title: 特征可视化与分析
nodes.label: 可解释性
nodes.summary: 使用反卷积方法可视化C3D学习的特征，发现早期层学习低级运动模式，后期层学习高级语义运动模式。
nodes.description: 可视化显示C3D在最初几帧捕获外观，之后只关注显著运动。在conv2a层学习边缘、斑块等低级运动，在conv3b层学习角点、纹理、身体部位等，在conv5b层学习更抽象的运动模式。

edges.label: 构成
edges.description: 3D卷积和池化操作是构建C3D网络架构的基础。

edges.label: 指导
edges.description: 架构搜索实验的结果（3×3×3同构最佳）直接指导了最终C3D网络的设计。

edges.label: 训练对象
edges.description: C3D网络架构是训练过程的对象。

edges.label: 模型来源
edges.description: 训练好的C3D模型用于推理时的特征提取。

edges.label: 分析对象
edges.description: 提取的C3D特征被用于可视化分析，以理解网络学习的内容。

deltas.before: 2D卷积网络在视频上应用时，时间信息在第一层卷积后就丢失了。
deltas.after: 3D卷积网络在所有层传播时间信息，能够同时建模外观和运动。
deltas.why_it_matters: 这是C3D能够学习有效时空特征的核心原因，使其在视频任务上优于2D特征。

deltas.before: 先前的3D ConvNet方法（如[15]）依赖人体检测和头部跟踪进行预处理，难以扩展到大规模数据集。
deltas.after: C3D直接以完整视频帧作为输入，无需预处理，易于扩展到大规模数据集。
deltas.why_it_matters: 简化了流程，使得在Sports-1M等大规模数据集上训练成为可能。

deltas.before: 视频描述符可能需要复杂的特征编码和分类器。
deltas.after: C3D特征与简单的线性分类器（如线性SVM）结合就能取得优异性能。
deltas.why_it_matters: 体现了C3D特征的判别性和简单性，便于实际应用。

deltas.before: iDT等手工特征计算密集，速度慢。
deltas.after: C3D特征提取速度极快，比iDT快91倍，比Brox光流GPU实现快274倍。
deltas.why_it_matters: 高效性对于大规模视频处理至关重要。

定义了3D卷积/池化核的尺寸，其中d是时间维度，k是空间维度。实验表明d=3, k=3（即3×3×3）效果最佳。

evidence.description: 架构搜索实验显示，深度-3（3D卷积）在UCF101上准确率显著高于深度-1（2D卷积）。

claims.claim: 具有小3×3×3卷积核的同构架构是3D ConvNets的最佳架构之一。
risk_flags: 搜索空间有限（主要变化时间深度），可能未探索其他潜在优秀架构。

evidence.description: 在UCF101上，深度-3的同构架构在准确率和参数效率上优于其他深度设置（深度-1、5、7）和变化深度架构。

risk_flags: 在Sports-1M和UCF101上未达到绝对最佳；需要与iDT结合才能在某些任务上超越双流网络。

evidence.description: 在UCF101上，C3D (3 nets) + iDT + linear SVM达到90.4%准确率，与最佳方法相当。
在ASLAN上，C3D + linear SVM达到78.3%准确率和86.5% AUC，显著优于当时最佳方法。
在YUPENN和Maryland场景识别上，C3D分别达到98.1%和87.7%准确率，达到或接近最佳。

claims.claim: C3D特征是紧凑、高效且简单的。
risk_flags: “简单”的评估较为主观；高效性是在特定硬件上测量的。

C3D特征提取速度比iDT快91倍，比Brox光流GPU实现快274倍，表明其高效性。

evidence.description: 反卷积可视化显示，C3D在早期层学习低级运动模式（边缘、斑块），在后期层学习高级语义运动模式（身体部位、轨迹、特定动作），表明其同时建模外观和运动。

terms.definition: Convolutional 3D，本文提出的3D卷积网络及其学习的视频特征。
3D卷积网络，使用3D卷积和3D池化操作在时空维度上进行特征学习的神经网络。
同时包含空间（外观）和时间（运动）信息的特征。
一个包含约110万体育视频、487个类别的大型视频分类数据集，用于训练C3D。
一个包含101个人类动作类别的中等规模动作识别数据集，用于架构搜索和评估。
improved Dense Trajectories，一种基于光流跟踪和低级梯度直方图的手工视频特征。
C3D网络中第一个全连接层的激活，通常用作视频特征。
一种可视化技术，用于将网络高层激活投影回图像空间，以理解网络学习的内容。

required_datasets.name: Sports-1M
required_datasets.availability: 公开，但下载和处理大规模视频数据需要大量存储和计算资源。

required_models.name: C3D模型
required_models.availability: 论文作者提供了预训练模型和源代码。

reproduction.required_compute: 需要GPU进行训练，特别是Sports-1M数据集上的训练需要大量计算资源。论文未明确说明具体GPU型号和训练时间，但提到训练是耗时的。
reproduction.code_available: 是，作者提供了源代码和预训练模型：http://vlg.cs.dartmouth.edu/c3d

steps.description: 1. 下载Sports-1M数据集并进行预处理（提取2秒片段，调整大小，裁剪）。
2. 按照论文描述实现C3D网络架构（8个3×3×3卷积层，5个池化层，2个全连接层）。
3. 在Sports-1M训练集上使用SGD训练网络（初始学习率0.003，每150K迭代除以2，训练1.9M迭代）。
4. 训练完成后，使用网络提取视频特征：将视频分成16帧重叠片段，提取fc6激活，平均并L2归一化。
5. 在下游任务（如UCF101动作识别）上，使用提取的C3D特征训练线性SVM分类器进行评估。

metadata.title: Learning Spatiotemporal Features with 3D Convolutional Networks
metadata.venue: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision
metadata.paper_type: Computer Vision / CNN / Top-cited ML method paper

anchors.text_span: Learning Spatiotemporal Features with 3D Convolutional Networks Du Tran1,2, Lubomir Bourdev1, Rob Fergus1, Lorenzo Torresani2, Manohar Paluri1 1Facebook AI Research, 2Dartmouth College {dutran,lorenzo}@cs.dartmouth.edu {lubomir,robfergus,mano}@fb.com
Abstract
We propose a simple, yet effective approach for spa- tiotemporal feature learning using deep 3-dimensional con-
volutional networks (3D ConvNets) trained on a large scale

supervised video dataset. Our ﬁndings are three-fold: 1) 3D ConvNets are more suitable for spatiotemporal feature learning compared to 2D ConvNets; 2) A homogeneous ar- chitecture with small 3 × 3 × 3 convolution kernels in all
layers is among the best performing architectures for 3D

ConvNets; and 3) Our learned features, namely C3D (Con- volutional 3D), with a simple linear classiﬁer outperform state-of-the-art methods on 4 different benchmarks and are comparable with current best methods on the other 2 bench- marks. In addition, the features are compact: achieving 52.8% accuracy on UCF101 dataset with only 10 dimen- sions and also very efﬁcient to compute due to the fast in- ference of ConvNets. Finally, they are conceptually very simple and easy to train and use. 1. Introduction Multimedia on the Internet is growing rapidly result- ing in an increasing number of videos being shared every
minute. To combat the information explosion it is essen-

tial to understand and analyze these videos for various pur- poses like search, recommendation, ranking etc. The com- puter vision community has been working on video analysis for decades and tackled different problems such as action recognition [26], abnormal event detection [2], and activity understanding [23]. Considerable progress has been made in these individual problems by employing different spe- ciﬁc solutions. However, there is still a growing need for
a generic video descriptor that helps in solving large-scale
video tasks in a homogeneous way. There are four properties for an effective video descrip- tor: (i) it needs to be generic, so that it can represent differ-
ent types of videos well while being discriminative. For ex-

ample, Internet videos can be of landscapes, natural scenes, sports, TV shows, movies, pets, food and so on; (ii) the de- scriptor needs to be compact: as we are working with mil- lions of videos, a compact descriptor helps processing, stor- ing, and retrieving tasks much more scalable; (iii) it needs to be efﬁcient to compute, as thousands of videos are expected
to be processed every minute in real world systems; and

(iv) it must be simple to implement. Instead of using com- plicated feature encoding methods and classiﬁers, a good descriptor should work well even with a simple model (e.g. linear classiﬁer). Inspired by the deep learning breakthroughs in the image domain [24] where rapid progress has been made in the past few years in feature learning, various pre-trained convolu- tional network (ConvNet) models [16] are made available for extracting image features. These features are the activa- tions of the network’s last few fully-connected layers which perform well on transfer learning tasks [47, 48]. However, such image based deep features are not directly suitable for videos due to lack of motion modeling (as shown in our experiments in sections 4,5,6). In this paper we propose to learn spatio-temporal features using deep 3D ConvNet. We empirically show that these learned features with a sim- ple linear classiﬁer can yield good performance on various video analysis tasks. Although 3D ConvNets...
ConvNets in the context of large-scale supervised training

datasets and modern deep architectures to achieve the best performance on different types of video analysis tasks. The features from these 3D ConvNets encapsulate information related to objects, scenes and actions in a video, making them useful for various tasks without requiring to ﬁnetune the model for each task. C3D has the properties that a good descriptor should have: it is generic, compact, simple and efﬁcient. To summarize, our contributions in this paper are: • We experimentally show 3D convolutional deep net- works are good feature learning machines that model appearance and motion simultaneously. • We empirically ﬁnd that 3 × 3 × 3 convolution kernel for all layers to work best among the limited set of explored architectures. • The proposed features with a simple linear model out- perform or approach the current best methods on4 dif- ferent tasks and 6 different benchmarks (see Table 1). Related Work Videos have been studied by the computer vision com- munity for decades. Over the years various problems like action recognition [26], anomaly detection [2], video re- trieval [1], event and action detection [30, 17], and many more have been proposed. Considerable portion of these works are about video representations. Laptev and Linde- berg [26] proposed spatio-temporal interest points (STIPs) by extending Harris corner detectors to 3D. SIFT and HOG are also extended into SIFT- 3D [34] and HOG3D [19] for action recognition. Dollar et al. proposed Cuboids features for behavior recognition [5]. Sadanand and Corso built Ac- tionBank for action recognition [33]. Recently, Wang et al. proposed improved Dense Trajectories (...
computationally intensive and becomes intractable on large-
scale datasets. With recent availability of powerful parallel machines
(GPUs, CPU clusters), together with large amounts of train-

ing data, convolutional neural networks (ConvNets) [28] have made a come back providing breakthroughs on visual recognition [10, 24]. ConvNets have also been applied to the problem of human pose estimation in both images [12] and videos [13]. More interestingly these deep networks are used for image feature learning [7]. Similarly, Zhou et al. and perform well on transferred learning tasks. Deep learning has also been applied to video feature learning in an unsupervised setting [27]. In Le et al. [27], the au- thors use stacked ISA to learn spatio-temporal features for videos. Although this method showed good results on ac- tion recognition, it is still computationally intensive at train-
ing and hard to scale up for testing on large datasets. 3D

ConvNets were proposed for human action recognition [15] and for medical image segmentation [14, 42]. 3D convo- lution was also used with Restricted Boltzmann Machines to learn spatiotemporal features [40]. Recently, Karpathy et
al. [18] trained deep networks on a large video dataset for

video classiﬁcation. Simonyan and Zisserman [36] used two stream networks to achieve best results on action recog- nition. Among these approaches, the 3D ConvNets approach in [15] is most closely related to us. This method used a hu- man detector and head tracking to segment human subjects in videos. The segmented video volumes are used as inputs for a 3-convolution-layer 3D ConvNet to classify actions. In contrast, our method takes full video frames as inputs and does not rely on any preprocessing, thus easily scaling to
large datasets. We also share some similarities with Karpa-

thy et al. [18] and Simonyan and Zisserman [36] in terms of using full frames for training the ConvNet. However, these methods are built on using only 2D convolution and 2D pooling operations (except for the Slow Fusion model in [18]) whereas our model performs 3D convolutions and 3D pooling propagating temporal information across all the layers in the network (further detailed in section 3). We also show that gradually pooling space and time information and building deeper networks achieves best results and we dis- cuss more about the architecture search in section 3.2. 3. Learning Features with 3D ConvNets In this section we explain in detail the basic operations of 3D ConvNets, analyze different architectures for 3D Con-
vNets empirically, and elaborate how to train them on large-

scale datasets for feature learning. 3.1. 3D convolution and pooling We believe that3D ConvNet is well-suited for spatiotem- poral feature learning. Compared to 2D ConvNet, 3D Con- vNet has the ability to model temporal information better owing to 3D convolution and 3D pooling operations. In 3D ConvNets, convolution and pooling operations are per- formed spatio-temporally while in 2D ConvNets they are done only spatially. Figure 1 illustrates the difference, 2D convolution applied on an image will output an image, 2D convolution applied on multiple images (treating them as different channels [36]) also results in an image. Hence, 2D ConvNets lose temporal information of the input sig- nal right after every convolution operation. Only 3D con- volution preserves the temporal information of the input signals resulting in an output volume. The same phenom- ena is applicable for 2D and 3D polling. In [36], although

Simi- larly, fusion models in [18] used 2D convolutions, most of the networks lose their input’s temporal signal after the ﬁrst convolution layer. Only the Slow Fusion model in [18] uses 3D convolutions and averaging pooling in its ﬁrst 3 convo- lution layers. We believe this is the key reason why it per- forms best among all networks studied in [18]. However, it still loses all temporal information after the third convolu- tion layer. Figure 9 and 10 visualize deconvolutions of C3D learned

feature maps at the layers conv2a and conv3b. Visual- izations of the same feature map are grouped together. For ﬁgures 11, 12, 13, and 14, each ﬁgure presents the deconvo- lutions of one learned feature map of theconv5b layer. Fi- nally, ﬁgure 15 compares the deconvolutions of several C3D conv5b feature maps with optical ﬂows. As showed in the visualizations, at early convolution layerconv2a, C3D learns low-level motion patterns such as moving edges, blobs, short changes, edge orientation changes, or color changes. At a higher layer of conv3b, C3D learns bigger moving patterns of corners, textures, body parts, and trajec- tories. Finally, at the deepest convolution layer, conv5b, C3D learns more complicated motion patterns such as mov- ing circular objects, biking-like motions.
